desc.concept: coordinating or modal function words (or, can, but, would)
desc.note: Mixed function words; the largest group is " or" (9 of 20), with " can" and " but" also recurring. Windows with "at", "with", "science" and "view" are not counted.

desc.concept: mixed single-token fragments with no unifying theme
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous: gap/search/encoding/docs/championship/rxjs etc., no shared feature.

desc.concept: contrastive conjunctions 'but', 'or', 'yet' joining clauses
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly 'but' (8) and 'or' (8), plus 'yet' (2) and 'or'/'but' variants; 'yet' and 'but' are conjunction-family items; the remaining 3 (_id, white, law) are unrelated.

desc.concept: the word "or" as a disjunction in lists and alternatives
desc.note: Marked tokens are very diverse; "or" covers only 9 of 20 windows, so the unit is mostly token-specific with no single clear topic.

desc.concept: the word 'or' in alternatives and conjunctions
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly diverse; 'or' accounts for 8 of 21 windows, the largest single feature, with no other coherent family.

desc.concept: the conjunction "but" or "or" between clauses
desc.note: Windows split across several token types; the largest group is the " but"/" or" conjunctions (9 windows), with newlines and other tokens scattered.

desc.concept: comma punctuation
comma after a clause or list item, mid-sentence
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly commas; the 14 comma windows are the largest single feature, but comma fit is only 14/22 (about 64%), so the concept is a broad token rather than a topic.

desc.concept: commas and list/clause separators (mixed contexts)
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous: commas (8), digits (2), and singletons across unrelated contexts. Commas alone cover only about a third of windows, so no single concept fits well.

desc.concept: comma punctuation
desc.note: Marked tokens are mixed: comma (9), copula 'be' forms (are, was, been, be; 6), and prepositions at/from/by (4); the comma is the largest single feature, so the unit is scored on that.

desc.concept: mixed unrelated tokens; no shared feature
desc.note: Marked tokens (5, =, \$, the, recent, à, cript, Mark, to, Memory, :, he, IVE, ich, números, newline, snap, /, in) share no common concept across windows; frequency table lists only 12 distinct types and the windows are heterogeneous.

desc.concept: comma after introductory or parenthetical phrase
comma after clause or list item
desc.note: Non-comma marked tokens (K, Current, unn, injury, 2, devices, as, ak) are scattered and unrelated; the comma token dominates.

desc.concept: commas and other punctuation inside text
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly a comma or other punctuation, but many windows mark unrelated tokens, so the feature is diffuse.

desc.concept: commas and line breaks within varied text
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly commas, plus a few newlines and mixed items (men, women, people, manganese); no single coherent concept.

desc.concept: scattered unrelated tokens with no shared concept
desc.note: Marked tokens are all different (each appears once); windows span body, blog, tissue, margin, sugar, nebula, FM, Channel, etc. with no common feature.

desc.concept: comma token, mostly separating clauses or list items
desc.note: Comma dominates; a few windows mark ' or', ' by', ' at' instead

desc.concept: comma punctuation mid-sentence
desc.note: Marked token counts list 15 commas plus one each of six other tokens (prosec, href, BASIS, _object, other, semicolon), totaling 21 but 22 windows are given; fit uses 15 of 22 as the comma windows, and the sixth other token is one window with no token counted.

desc.concept: commas and punctuation marks, mixed contexts
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous: commas plus scattered tokens (clinical, were, 's, buffer, cuffs, MON, up); no single shared concept.

desc.concept: commas, plus 'women'/'people' nouns, mixed syntax
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly commas and a few person-nouns; no single coherent concept covers them.

desc.concept: copular "is" linking subject to predicate
the token "is" in varied contexts
desc.note: Windows are heterogeneous; the " is" token dominates but the sense varies (copula, 'Hell is other people', 'what is needed'). Other marked tokens are scattered singletons.

desc.concept: forms of the verb 'is' (copula/linking verb)
desc.note: Frequency table shows 8 ' is' marks out of 20 windows, which are not all in the table as listed; the count reflects the stated table, and the remaining marks are scattered unrelated tokens.

desc.concept: forms of 'be' copula, mostly 'is'
desc.note: Dominant token 'is' (10 of 21); other marked tokens are prepositions and miscellaneous words, so the unit is weaker on those.

desc.concept: mixed unrelated tokens, no shared theme
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous: ' setting', ' event', ' N', '0', ' outcome', '.hidden', ' dr', ' not', ' $' (x2), 'ave', ' Auto', ' a', ' MF', ' the', 'axes', '2', 'ience', 'By', '(extra' and '....' share no common concept.

desc.concept: copula "is" linking subject to predicate
forms of the copula "is" as the marked token
desc.note: Windows mostly mark " is" (13 of 25 windows, roughly 52%) but the 12 remaining marked tokens are unrelated (digits, "The", whitespace, comma, "goal", "hunters", colon), so this is a weak, mixed feature.

desc.concept: the copula "is" (mixed with a few other function words)
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous: 'is' appears 9 times, the remaining 12 are a scattered mix (Q, at, icons, ObjectType, have, for, repository, may, to, space, pulmonary), so the unit is not cleanly selective.

desc.concept: the word "is" as a copula in running text
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous: 8 of 21 are " is", the rest are unrelated single tokens (Return, Treasury, Tax, Gent, Radio, Out, Your, people, man, under, survey, demographic).

desc.concept: mixed unrelated tokens; no shared concept
desc.note: Every marked token is a different type with count 1, so no word family or topic recurs; the windows span unrelated domains.

desc.concept: copula "is" linking subject to predicate
desc.note: Windows mark forms of "is" (18 of 21 by the frequency table); the other three marks are "ekt" in "Detekt", a space, and " mother".

desc.concept: the copula 'is' linking subject to predicate
desc.note: Marked tokens are heterogeneous; 'is' occurs 11 times out of 20 windows (55% of frequency table entries are 'is', and the table lists 11 is-tokens of 20 total). Remaining windows mark unrelated tokens.

desc.concept: is/be/and/on: linking verbs and short function words
desc.note: Marked tokens are mostly a common copula ' is' plus assorted function words; no coherent shared concept, and the only recurring token covers under half the windows.

desc.concept: digits inside numbers and version/ID strings
desc.note: Activation is spread across many different tokens, mostly digits; the strongest shared feature is weak. Also fires on ' is' in 8 windows, but those are mixed with unrelated tokens.
